findings.resolution_hint: Rewrite each listed docstring's argument prose into the 'The arguments are:' bulleted list (one '- `name` — description.' bullet per positional and keyword argument), matching the already-compliant style used in e.g. Preflight.write_payloads and Preflight.render_args. Fix the two SCAN.ARGS_FORM bugs below first, then run `gbg scan docs --only SCAN.ARGS_FORM` to find every remaining instance mechanically rather than by hand, per RULE.DOC.CLASS_SWEEP.
findings.description: RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM requires the bulleted form led by 'The arguments are:' whenever a docstring documents three or more arguments OR any keyword argument at all; fewer than three with no keyword may stay in running prose, and the two forms are never mixed. I re-derived the real positional/keyword count from each function's own signature (stripping type annotations and defaults) and checked whether the docstring literally contains the bulleted marker 'The arguments are:' followed by a '- `name` — ...' list. After excluding the rule's own exemptions (an internal `_`-prefixed helper, a thin 'Allocating form of' wrapper, and a type docstring already carrying 'The fields are:') I count 74 docstrings across essentially every file of the src surface (TestHarness.jl, Witnesses.jl, Reflection.jl, Scan.jl, HtmlWalker.jl, TreeHash.jl, and ~19 of the 25 files under src/CLI/) that take 3+ arguments or at least one keyword argument, yet are documented in a single running-prose sentence of the form "The arguments are `x`, ...; `y`, ...; and `z`, ..." instead of the required bulleted list. This is precisely the pattern the package's own SCAN.ARGS_FORM (added 2026-09-09, per its header comment, because 'the rule had no enforcer anywhere') is built to catch, and it is the single largest class of findings on this surface — a self-application gap the tool has not yet run/fixed against its own source (consistent with the CLAUDE.md 'Current state' note that Phase 1 self-tests and the first release candidate are still pending).
findings.title: ~74 docstrings violate RULE.DOC.ARGS_FORM's bulleted-form rule

findings.description: SCAN.ARGS_FORM detects the bulleted form by a plain `occursin("The arguments are:", d.body)` substring test. `d.body` is the raw docstring text with its original line breaks, so this test fails whenever the source happens to wrap the phrase — 'The' ending one line and 'arguments are:' beginning the next, which the hanging-indent line width naturally produces. Two of the tool's OWN docstrings already do this by accident and are otherwise perfectly correctly bulleted: `Scan.prose_text` (src/Scan.jl:229-238) and `Preflight.write_payloads` (src/CLI/Preflight.jl:317-333) both write proper '- `name` — ...' lists, yet the literal marker they open with is split across a line break, so `bulleted` evaluates false for both. Since both functions take 3 (write_payloads: cfg, instrument, round, roster + base kw) or 1+1kw (prose_text: cfg, file + history_cut) arguments, `wants_bullets` is true, so the scan would emit a false-positive FAIL hit against docstrings that already comply with the rule — undermining the very sweep meant to fix finding 1.
findings.title: SCAN.ARGS_FORM false-positives when its own trigger phrase line-wraps

locations: src/Scans/args_form.jl:16 — "o = findfirst('(', sig); c = findlast(')', sig)"
src/Reflection.jl:154-166 — argcov(cfg; exempt = (hit -> false)) -> (hits, population, skipped)
findings.resolution_hint: Strip the return annotation the same way Reflection.argcov does: `sig = replace(d.signature, r"\s*->.*$" => "")` before computing `o`/`c`, or reuse `Reflection.argcov`'s stripped-signature logic directly.
findings.description: `Reflection.argcov` itself strips the return-type arrow first (`sig = replace(d.signature, r"\s*->.*$" => "")`, src/Reflection.jl:172) before locating the parameter list, precisely because a parenthesised return annotation would otherwise be mistaken for part of the signature. `SCAN.ARGS_FORM` (src/Scans/args_form.jl:16) skips this step and calls `findlast(')', sig)` on the raw signature line, so for any docstring whose return annotation is itself a parenthesised tuple, `c` lands on the closing paren of the RETURN tuple rather than the argument list's. Concretely, for argcov's own displayed signature `argcov(cfg; exempt = (hit -> false)) -> (hits, population, skipped)`, `inside` becomes `"cfg; exempt = (hit -> false)) -> (hits, population, skipped"`, and `Reflection.signature_parameters` then reads the return-tuple's element names `population` and `skipped` as two additional spurious keyword arguments (both parse as bare identifiers after the `=`-split). `argcov` genuinely has exactly one keyword (`exempt`); if this docstring is ever flagged (it currently is not being reached since the prose-vs-bulleted mismatch already applies for other reasons, but the message text is computed regardless of the branch taken), the printed hit would read '...takes 1 positional and 3 keyword argument(s)...' instead of the true 1-and-1. The same corruption applies to `Rounds.load(cfg, round) -> (dir, record)`, `Rounds.classify_lane(...) -> (status, data, sha, note)`, `Demote.demote(verdict) -> (verdict′, demoted::Bool)` and every other docstring in this codebase whose return arrow is a tuple (a very common style here).
findings.title: SCAN.ARGS_FORM does not strip the `-> ...` return annotation before parsing the parameter list
